disease_label_per_paper: Acute cholangitis secondary to gallstones with atypical chest pain and cough presentation
presentation_summary: 84-year-old woman presented with right-sided lower chest pain and cough rather than classic RUQ pain and fever.
On presentation she was afebrile, HR 120 bpm, RR 25/min, BP 130/70 mmHg, oxygen saturation 95% on room air, diaphoretic, acutely distressed, and jaundiced with scleral icterus.
Labs showed WBC 25.4/mm3 with 94.8% segmented neutrophils and 34% bandemia, total bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 3.6 mg/dL, ALP 144 U/L, AST 361 U/L, ALT 201 U/L, lipase 33 U/L, GGT 139 U/L.
Chest X-ray was negative. CT abdomen showed marked common bile duct dilation to about 2.9 cm due to a large non-radiopaque stone.
Blood cultures later showed Klebsiella variicola bacteremia; ERCP found two large lower-CBD stones, extracted one stone and placed a plastic biliary stent.
